title: Lost luggage
persona: You are a warm, chatty baggage services agent at Sydney Airport. You use Australian expressions like 'no worries' and 'mate', and you speak at a natural, quick pace.
briefTr: Sidney'e indin ama bavulun banttan çıkmadı. Büyük, siyah, kırmızı kurdeleli bir bavul. Harbour Hotel'de kalıyorsun. Adın {name}.
opening: G'day! Next please. How can I help you?

facts.question: Within how many hours should your bag arrive?
facts.questionTr: Bavulunun kaç saat içinde gelmesi bekleniyordu?

goals.instruction: The traveller says their suitcase did not arrive or is missing.
goals.successReply: Oh no, sorry to hear that.
goals.retryReply: What's the problem, mate? Is something missing?

goals.titleTr: Biniş kartını ve bagaj etiketini göstermek
goals.ask: Can I see your boarding pass and baggage tag?
goals.instruction: The traveller hands over the boarding pass and baggage tag.
goals.hint: Here are my boarding pass and baggage tag.
goals.hintTr: İşte biniş kartım ve bagaj etiketim.
goals.retryReply: I need your boarding pass and the baggage tag from check-in.

goals.instruction: The traveller describes the bag: colour, size, type, marks.
goals.hint: It's a large black suitcase with a red ribbon.
goals.hintTr: Büyük, siyah, kırmızı kurdeleli bir bavul.
goals.successReply: Got it, I'll put that in the system.
goals.retryReply: What does your bag look like? Colour, size?

goals.ask: So, have you been to Australia before?
goals.instruction: The agent makes friendly small talk. The traveller answers whether they have been to Australia before.
goals.hint: No, it's my first time in Australia.
goals.retryReply: Just curious — have you been here before?

goals.ask: Where are you staying in Sydney?
goals.instruction: The traveller says where to deliver the bag.
goals.hint: Please deliver it to the Harbour Hotel.
goals.successReply: No worries, we'll bring it to you.
goals.retryReply: Where should we deliver it when we find it?

goals.ask: We'll call you as soon as it turns up.
goals.instruction: The traveller asks for a reference number or a copy of the claim.
goals.hint: Can I have a reference number?
goals.successReply: Sure — your reference number is {ref}. It should arrive within {hours}.
goals.retryReply: Is there anything you need from me before you go?

goals.ask: Anything else I can do for you?
goals.instruction: The traveller asks if the airline will pay for essentials like clothes or a toothbrush.
goals.hint: Can I buy some clothes? Will you pay for them?
goals.hintTr: Biraz kıyafet alabilir miyim? Ücretini siz öder misiniz?
goals.successReply: Yes — keep your receipts and we'll pay you back.

twists.intro: Ah, found it in the system — your bag went to Melbourne by mistake.
twists.instruction: The bag is in another city. The traveller asks when it will arrive, asks for delivery to the hotel, or asks how this happened.
twists.retryReply: Sorry about that, mate. These things happen.

options.reply: It'll be on the first flight tomorrow morning.

options.text: Can you send it straight to my hotel?
options.reply: Absolutely, we'll deliver it to your hotel.
A tag mix-up in Istanbul, by the look of it. Sorry!

twists.intro: Oh, wait — your bag just came in. But one of the wheels is broken.
twists.instruction: The bag arrived damaged. The traveller asks for a repair, compensation, or a damage report.
twists.retryReply: I'm really sorry. How would you like to handle it?

options.reply: Yes, we'll repair it for free and bring it to your hotel.

options.text: Can I get compensation for the damage?
options.reply: Yes, just fill in this damage form and we'll pay you back.

options.text: I'd like to make a damage report, please.
options.reply: Of course, here's the report form.

twists.intro: We have a black suitcase here with no tag. Is this yours?
twists.instruction: A similar bag was found. The traveller checks it: it is not theirs, asks to look at it, or points out their red ribbon.

options.text: No, mine has a red ribbon.
options.reply: Ah, not yours then. We'll keep looking.

options.text: Can I have a closer look?
options.reply: Sure — hmm, no ribbon. Not yours.

twists.intro: Just so you know, you'll need to fill in the claim online. Here's the website.
twists.instruction: The claim must be filed online. The traveller asks for help, asks for a paper form, or asks if the website is in other languages.
twists.retryReply: Most people do it on their phone, it's quick.

options.text: Can you help me fill it in?
options.reply: Of course, let's do it together right now.

options.text: Can I have a paper form instead?
options.reply: Sure, I've got a paper one here.
Not Turkish, sorry, but it's very simple English.

twists.intro: Just a heads up — we only pay for things you buy after the first 24 hours.
twists.instruction: Purchases on the first day are not covered. The traveller asks why, asks what is covered, or asks for an exception.

options.reply: Most bags turn up within a day. But I'll note your case.
Toiletries and basic clothes, up to a hundred dollars a day.

options.text: Can you make an exception? I have nothing to wear.
options.reply: Let me talk to my manager… Okay, we'll cover a toothbrush and a shirt today.

twists.intro: Between you and me, it might take two days.
twists.instruction: The delivery may take two days. The traveller asks for updates, asks for faster delivery, or asks for a tracking link.

options.reply: Yes, you'll get a text every time it moves.

options.text: Is there any way to make it faster?
options.reply: I'll mark it urgent. That usually helps.
Yes, use your reference number on our website.

closing: Hang in there, {name} — we'll find it. Enjoy Sydney!
